display_name: Tyrrell's Vat 1 Semillon, New South Wales
raw_content:
{
  "hook": "Vines planted in 1867 on Hunter Valley's sandy alluvial loam deliver Tyrrell's Vat 1 Semillon's core of low-yield concentration. Neutral oak aging lets terroir-driven lanolin and emerging toast dominate without oak interference. This setup explains the wine's waxy persistence that outlasts flashier whites.",
  "wine_summary": "Tyrrell's Vat 1 stands as Hunter Valley's longest continuously produced Semillon, sourced from their Pokolbin estate vines averaging 120 years old. The producer's focus on dry-farmed old sites preserves Semillon's varietal purity amid the region's humid challenges. These factors yield a wine that tracks Australia's shift toward ageworthy whites, with vintages like 2016 earning TEXSOM gold.",
  "terroir_expression": "Hunter Valley's sandy alluvial loam and friable red duplex soils force deep roots in this subtropical climate of hot days and humid summers, concentrating Semillon's lemon and fig into waxy density. The Great Dividing Range's shelter tempers rainfall, while river proximity adds humidity that promotes early ripening and moderate acidity. This geology translates to lanolin grip and toast evolution in the glass.",
  "vinification_summary": "Hand-harvested fruit undergoes wild yeast fermentation in used French oak barriques, followed by extended lees contact for textural breadth. Neutral vessels avoid new oak flavors, preserving site expression; this barrel lees aging technique builds oxidative complexity without fortification. Choices suit Semillon's low-acid profile, enhancing beeswax development over 5-10 years.",
  "food_pairing": "Roast chicken with garlic and lemon—waxy body coats the crispy skin while acidity slices herbal fat. Nashville hot chicken counters spice with cooling lanolin and toast. Lobster thermidor matches richness to cream sauce via beeswax viscosity. Aged Comté cheese amplifies nutty toast parallels. Veal piccata's capers echo emerging minerality against butter.",
  "comparable_wines": "Brokenwood Hunter Valley Semillon — old-vine Hunter focus yields parallel wax and age potential. Jim Barry The Lodge Hill Semillon — Clare Valley counterpart with similar lanolin from friable loams.",
  "style_profile": "Medium-bodied dry white with waxy texture and toasty aging arc",
  "cellar_recommendation": "Open 2016 after 8 years for peak toast; 2007 drinks now. Store at 55°F in darkness to sustain development through 2040.",
  "value_assessment": "$60 at Wally's for 2015 aligns with Brokenwood Graveyard Parcel Semillon. Tyrrell's Vat 1 justifies the price through unmatched vine age and 20-year track record. It beats Bordeaux Semillon blends on purity and persistence.",
  "market_position": "Sommeliers in coastal US restaurants list vintages by-the-glass for Semillon education. Auction houses move 2007 lots to Australian collectors. Retail targets oenophiles scanning Hunter sections.",
  "insider_take": "Drinkers fixate on young citrus and miss Vat 1's transformation into honeyed beeswax after a decade. The tradeoff: upfront accessibility yields to profound depth, so cellaring beats quaffing. Skip if oxidative notes repel you.",
  "aging_potential_years": 25,
  "drinking_window_min_years": 5,
